page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7.8xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor and x86_64 architecture. It features an Intel Xeon 8369B processor operating at 2.7 GHz, configured with 16 physical cores and 32 virtual cores (vCPUs) via hyperthreading. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 16 Gbps.

Benchmark data places the ecs.r7.8xlarge in the average tier for most compute and memory operations. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance score is 1865.39, and the multi-core score is 30983.52. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block cached speed of 1689.81 GB/sec and a large block uncached write speed of 65.94 GB/sec. In database and key-value store operations, the instance achieves 30.13 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks. Notably, the instance demonstrates strong performance in small-scale language model text generation, delivering 282.15 tokens per second with a 135M parameter model, though performance scales down to an average of 17.54 tokens per second for a 7B parameter model.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.r7.8xlarge offers a dense memory allocation relative to its processing cores, making it suitable for memory-bound workloads without paying for excess compute resources. However, the complete absence of local storage represents a key tradeoff, as users must provision and pay for external block storage, which may introduce latency and additional network overhead. The instance is suited for enterprise databases, in-memory caching layers like Redis, medium-scale web serving, and memory-intensive data processing tasks.
